## 9.3 Collective Communication APIs

## 9.3.1 API Overview

The high-level API NPUDistributedOptimizer enables the user to automatically complete gradient aggregation without sensing AllReduce, implementing data parallel training. In addition, to meet users' requirements for flexibility, the API for atomic communication in collective communication is provided to implement native representation of data parallelism.

Currently, the AllReduce, Broadcast, AllGather, ReduceScatter, Send, as well as the Receive operations are supported, and a process group that participates in collective communication can be customized. For example, eight processors can be divided into groups of four for collective communication. Collective communication provides common APIs such as rank management, gradient segmentation, and collective communication prototype.

Table 9-1 Terminology

breadcrumb: [Doc: TensorFlowNetworkModelPortingandTrainingGuide > Section: 9 More Functions > 9.3 Collective Communication APIs > 9.3.1 API Overview]
content:
[Doc: TensorFlowNetworkModelPortingandTrainingGuide > 9 More Functions > 9.3 Collective Communication APIs > 9.3.1 API Overview]

The high-level API NPUDistributedOptimizer enables the user to automatically complete gradient aggregation without sensing AllReduce, implementing data parallel training. In addition, to meet users' requirements for flexibility, the API for atomic communication in collective communication is provided to implement native representation of data parallelism.
Currently, the AllReduce, Broadcast, AllGather, ReduceScatter, Send, as well as the Receive operations are supported, and a process group that participates in collective communication can be customized. For example, eight processors can be divided into groups of four for collective communication. Collective communication provides common APIs such as rank management, gradient segmentation, and collective communication prototype.
Table 9-1 Terminology

| Term           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ranktable file | Describes the information of the cluster involved in collective communication, including the organization information about the servers, devices, and containers.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Rank           | Indicates the processes that participate in collective communication.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Group          | Indicates the process group that participates in collective communication. The process group includes: ● HCCL world group: default global group, including all ranks that participate in collective communication. The group is created using the ranktable file. ● Custom group: a subset of the process groups contained in the HCCL world group. The ranks in the ranktable can be defined as different groups through the create_group API, and the collective communication algorithms can be executed in parallel. |
| Term                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|-----------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Rank size             | ● Rank size: indicates the number of ranks in a group. The maximum value is 4096. ● Local rank size: indicates the number of ranks in a group on the server where the processes are located. The value can be 1, 2, 4 or 8.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Rank ID               | ● Rank ID: indicates the ID of a process in a group. The value ranges from 0 to the value of rank size - 1. For a custom group, the rank starts from 0 in the group. For an HCCL world group, the rank ID is the same as the world rank ID. ● World rank ID: indicates the rank ID of a process in a HCCl world group. The value ranges from 0 to rank size - 1. ● Local rank ID: indicates the rank ID of a process in a group on the server where the process is located. The value ranges from 0 to local rank size - 1. |
| Gradient segmentation | In the backward pass phase of the neural network training, AllReduce of multiple parameters in the GE optimization computational graph is fused and segmented. AllReduce is performed segment by segment based on the gradient generation sequence to update the backward pass parameters of the network, implementing compute resource optimization, as well as parallel optimization of communication time and backward pass time.                                                                                        |

## 9.3.2 Initializing Collective Communication

If you call an HCCL API such as get_local_rank_id, get_rank_size, or get_rank_id before calling sess.run() or estimator.train(), you need to start another session and execute initialize_system to initialize collective communication. After the training is complete, execute shutdown_system and close the session.

breadcrumb: [Doc: TensorFlowNetworkModelPortingandTrainingGuide > Section: 9 More Functions > 9.3 Collective Communication APIs > 9.3.2 Initializing Collective Communication]

[Doc: TensorFlowNetworkModelPortingandTrainingGuide > 9 More Functions > 9.3 Collective Communication APIs > 9.3.2 Initializing Collective Communication]

```
import tensorflow as tf from npu_bridge.npu_init import * npu_int = npu_ops.initialize_system() npu_shutdown = npu_ops.shutdown_system() # If some specific functions need to be enabled during training, pass related arguments here. For details, see the description of the initialize_system API. config = tf.ConfigProto() custom_op = config.graph_options.rewrite_options.custom_optimizers.add() custom_op.name = "NpuOptimizer" custom_op.parameter_map["use_off_line"].b = True config.graph_options.rewrite_options.remapping = RewriterConfig.OFF # Disable remapping. init_sess = tf.Session(config=config) init_sess.run(npu_int) # Call an HCCL API... # Perform training. If another session is started to perform training, set the same run parameters as the preceding ones. init_sess.run(npu_shutdown) init_sess.close()
```

## 9.3.3 Specifying Devices to Perform Collective Communication

Call create_group to specify the devices that participate in collective communication. If this API is not called to create a custom group, all devices are created as the global hccl_world_group by default based on the ranktable file.

For example, you can select the first two devices in hccl_world_group as a group for collective communication:

from npu_bridge.npu_init import * create_group("myGroup", 2, [0, 1])

## 9.3.4 Obtaining the Group Information

You can call the group management API to obtain the group information.

get_rank_size: obtains the number of all devices in the current group. from npu_bridge.npu_init import * rankSize = get_rank_size("myGroup")

get_local_rank_size: obtains the number of devices in a group on the server where the current device is located.

from npu_bridge.npu_init import *

lcoalRankSize = get_local_rank_size("myGroup")

get_rank_id: obtains the logical device ID (rank ID) of the current device in a group. from npu_bridge.npu_init import * rankId = get_rank_id("myGroup")

get_local_rank_id: obtains the logical device ID (local rank ID) of the current device on the server.

from npu_bridge.npu_init import * localRankId = get_local_rank_id("myGroup")

## About Estimator

Estimator is a high-level API of TensorFlow and is introduced in TensorFlow 1.10 released in 2018. It greatly streamlines the programming process of machine learning. Estimator has many advantages, for example, good support for distribution, simplified model creation, and code sharing between model developers.

To use the Estimator API to develop a training script, perform the following steps.

Table 10-1 Training flow

Estimator is a high-level API of TensorFlow and is introduced in TensorFlow 1.10 released in 2018. It greatly streamlines the programming process of machine learning. Estimator has many advantages, for example, good support for distribution, simplified model creation, and code sharing between model developers.
To use the Estimator API to develop a training script, perform the following steps.
Table 10-1 Training flow

| Step                   | Description                                                                                                                        |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Preprocess the data.   | Create the input function input_fn.                                                                                                |
| Build a model.         | Construct the model function model_fn.                                                                                             |
| Set run configuration. | Instantiate Estimator and pass an object of the Runconfig class as the run parameter.                                              |
| Start training.        | Call the training method Estimator.train() in Estimator to train the model with a fixed number of steps using the specified input. |

## Directory Files
Table 10-2 PY file description

| File Name                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| imagenet_main.py          | Includes APIs related to ImageNet preprocessing, model construction definition, and model runtime. The get_filenames(), parse_record(), input_fn(), get_synth_input_fn(), and _parse_example_proto() functions are used for data preprocessing. The ImagenetModel class, imagenet_model_fn(), run_cifar(), and define_cifar_flags() functions are used for model operations. |
| imagenet_preprocessing.py | Includes ImageNet image data preprocessing APIs for sampling training images with the provided bounding box, cropping images based on the bounding box, randomly flipping images, and adjusting images to the target output size (the aspect ratio is not retained). Image resizing (aspect ratio retained) and central cropping are used during the evaluation process.     |
| resnet_model.py           | Implements the ResNet model, including the auxiliary functions for ResNet model construction and ResNet block definition functions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| File Name          | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
|--------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| resnet_run_loop.py | Model runtime file, including input processing and run loop. Input processing includes decoding the input data, converting the format, outputting image and label, as well as setting data randomization, batch, and pre-reading based on whether it is the training scenario. Run loop includes constructing Estimator, and performing training and validation. In general, the model is run in specific environments to implement data and error flow, so that model parameters can be updated using gradient descent. |

## 10.2.2 TF Adapter APIs

## 10.2.2.1 Overview

Since TF Adapter provides APIs adapted to the TensorFlow framework, you can develop TensorFlow-based training scripts.

Figure 10-1 TF Adapter

To use TF Adapter, the TFPlugin software package must be installed.

- If the --pylocal mode is used for the installation of TFPlugin, the corresponding .whl is installed in /tfplugin/python/site-packages/ in the TFPlugin installation path.
- If the --pylocal mode is not used to for the installation of TFPlugin, the corresponding .whl is installed in the local Python path.

Restrictions
Parameters
In multi-device training scenarios, the save_checkpoints_secs parameter cannot be used to save files by time.

| Parameter                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NPURunConfig parameters inherited from RunConfig: | NPURunConfig parameters inherited from RunConfig:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| model_dir                                         | Path of the model. Defaults to None. If model_dir set in NPURunConfig and NPUEstimator are different, an error is reported. If either NPURunConfig or NPUEstimator is configured with model_dir, the configured path applies. If neither NPURunConfig nor NPUEstimator is configured with model_dir, a model_dir_xxxxxxxxxx directory is created in the current script execution path to save the model file. |
| tf_random_seed                                    | Seed of the initialization variable. Defaults to None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| save_summary_steps                                | Interval (in steps) for saving the summary file. Defaults to 0. Applies only to the scenario where iterations_per_loop = 1. If iterations_per_loop > 1, the configured value may not be saved. For details about how to save information, see "Log and Summary Operators".                                                                                                                                    |
| Parameter                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
|-------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| save_checkpoints_steps        | Interval (in steps) for saving the checkpoint file. Defaults to None. ● This parameter and save_checkpoints_secs are mutually exclusive. ● If save_checkpoints_steps and save_checkpoints_secs are set to None, the checkpoint file is saved every 100 steps. ● If the value of iterations_per_loop is greater than 1, the value of save_checkpoints_steps must be a positive integer multiple of iterations_per_loop; otherwise, checkpoint data is not saved as defined by save_checkpoints_steps. To save the checkpoint data on only a specific device, modify the training script as follows: Original TensorFlow code: self._classifier=tf.estimator.Estimator( model_fn=cnn_model_fn, model_dir=self._model_dir, config=tf.estimator.RunConfig( save_checkpoints_steps=50 if hvd.rank() == 0 else None, keep_checkpoint_max=1)) Code after migration: self._classifier=NPUEstimator( model_fn=cnn_model_fn, model_dir=self._model_dir, config=tf.estimator.NPURunConfig( save_checkpoints_steps=50 if rank_id == 0 else 0, keep_checkpoint_max=1)) |
| save_checkpoints_secs         | Interval (in seconds) for saving the checkpoint file. Defaults to None. This parameter and save_checkpoints_steps are mutually exclusive.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| session_config                | ConfigProto format object for session configuration. Defaults to None.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| keep_checkpoint_max           | Maximum number of checkpoint files that can be stored. Defaults to 5.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| keep_checkpoint_every_n_hours | Number of hours to retain the checkpoint file. Defaults to 10000. This function can be disabled. To use this function, set keep_checkpoint_max to a large value.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Parameter                                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|---------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| log_step_count_steps                                    | Interval (in steps) for recording the global step and loss values. Defaults to 100. Applies only to the scenario where iterations_per_loop = 1. If iterations_per_loop > 1, the configured value may not be saved. For details about how to save information, see "Log and Summary Operators". |
| NPURunConfig does not support the following parameters: | NPURunConfig does not support the following parameters:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| train_distribute                                        | Indicates whether to perform distributed training. The distributed configuration is specified by experimental_distribute. TF Adapter encapsulates the single-server training optimizer using the NPUDistributedOptimizer class, to construct an NPU distributed training optimizer.            |
| device_fn                                               | Obtains the function of the Device field of each operation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| protocol                                                | Protocol used to start the server. This parameter is optional. If the parameter is empty, the gRPC is used by default.                                                                                                                                                                         |
| eval_distribute                                         | Indicates whether to perform distributed evaluation. The distributed configuration is specified by experimental_distribute.                                                                                                                                                                    |
| experimental_distribute                                 | Distributed configuration                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| The following NPURunConfig parameters are added:        | The following NPURunConfig parameters are added:                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Parameter            | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| iterations_per_loop  | Number of iterations per training loop performed on the per sess.run() call. Defaults to 1. The total number of training iterations per loop must be an integer multiple of the value of iterations_per_loop. Training is performed according to the specified number of iterations per loop (iterations_per_loop) on the and then the result is returned to the host. This parameter can save unnecessary interactions between the host and device and reduce the training time consumption. In mixed computing mode (mix_compile_mode is set to True), this parameter must be set to 1. Note: When iterations_per_loop is set to a value greater than 1, the total number of training iterations set by the user may be different from the actual total number of iterations due to issues such as loop offloading and loss scale overflow. Example: config = NPURunConfig(iterations_per_loop=1000) |
| profiling_config     | Profiling switch. Before creating NPURunConfig, you can instantiate a ProfilingConfig class to configure profiling. For details about the constructor of the ProfilingConfig class, see 10.2.2.2.2 ProfilingConfig Constructor. Example: config = NPURunConfig(profiling_config=profiling_config)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| dump_config          | Dump switch. Before creating NPURunConfig, you can instantiate a DumpConfig class for dump configuration. For details about the constructor of the DumpConfig class, see 10.2.2.2.3 DumpConfig Constructor. Example: config = NPURunConfig(dump_config=dump_config)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| enable_data_pre_proc | Indicates whether to offload the data preprocessing workload to the device side. ● True (default): enabled ● False: disabled Example: config = NPURunConfig(enable_data_pre_proc=True)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Parameter                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
|--------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| precision_mode           | A string for the operator precision mode. ● allow_fp32_to_fp16 or None: If an operator does not support the float32 data type, the precision is reduced to float16. By default, this mode is selected. ● force_fp16: If an operator supports both float16 and float32 data types, float16 is forcibly selected. ● must_keep_origin_dtype: The original precision is retained. ● allow_mix_precision: Mixed precision is enabled. For operators of the float32 data type on a network, the precision of some float32 operators can be automatically reduced to float16 based on the built-in optimization policy. In this way, the system performance is improved and the memory usage is reduced with little accuracy loss. After this function is enabled, you can enable loss scaling to compensate for the accuracy drop caused by precision reduction. For details about the related APIs, see 10.2.2.6.1 NPULossScaleOptim- izer Constructor. Example: config = NPURunConfig(precision_mode="allow_mix_precision") |
| enable_reduce_precision  | This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| variable_format_optimize | Variable format optimization enable ● True (default): enabled ● False: disabled To improve training efficiency, during the initialization of network variables, the variables are converted into a data format that is more suitable for running on the . However, this function should be disabled in special scenarios. Example: config = NPURunConfig(variable_format_optimize=True)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Parameter                | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| mix_compile_mode         | Mixed computing enable ● True: enabled. ● False (default): disabled (fully offloaded mode) In fully offloaded mode, all compute operators are offloaded to the device side. As a supplement to the fully offloaded mode, mixed computing allows some operators to be executed online in the frontend framework, improving the flexibility for adapting to TensorFlow. Example: config = NPURunConfig(mix_compile_mode=True)                         |
| hcom_parallel            | Whether to enable the AllReduce gradient update and forward and backward parallel execution. ● True: enabled ● False (default): disabled Example: config = NPURunConfig(hcom_parallel=True)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| graph_memory_max_size    | Network static memory and maximum dynamic memory, which can be specified based on the network size. The value ranges from 0 to 256 x 1024 x 1024 x 1024 or 0 to 274877906944, in bytes. Due to Ascend AI Processor hardware restrictions, the sum of graph_memory_max_size and variable_memory_max_size cannot exceed 31 GB. If not set, 26 GB is used by default. Example: config = NPURunConfig(graph_memory_max_size=str(26*1024 * 1024 * 1024)) |
| variable_memory_max_size | Variable memory, which can be specified based on the network size. The value ranges from 0 to 256 x 1024 x 1024 x 1024 or 0 to 274877906944, in bytes. Due to Ascend AI Processor hardware restrictions, the sum of graph_memory_max_size and variable_memory_max_size cannot exceed 31 GB. If not set, 5 GB is used by default. Example: config = NPURunConfig(variable_memory_max_size=str(5*1024 * 1024 * 1024))                                 |
| Parameter               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| auto_tune_mode          | You can determine whether to use the Auto Tune tool to tune the TBE operators during build to find the best performance configuration on the . ● Genetic Algorithm (GA): configures the tuning performance of the Cube operator. ● Reinforcement Learning (RL): sets vector operator tuning performance. You can specify both modes. Enclose the whole argument in double quotation marks (""), and separate the modes by commas (,). If not specified, Auto Tune is disabled. For details about the usage of the Auto Tune tool, see "Auto Tune Tool Instructions" in CANN Auxiliary Development Tool Guide. Example: config = NPURunConfig(auto_tune_mode="RL,GA") |
| stream_max_parallel_num | AI CPU and AI Core engine parallelism for parallel execution of AI CPU and AI Core operators. Example: config = NPURunConfig(stream_max_parallel_num="DNN_VM_TF: 10,DNN_V100:1") DNN_VM_TF is the name of the AI CPU engine. In this example, the number of concurrent tasks of the AI CPU engine is 10. DNN_V100 is the name of the AI Core engine. In this example, the number of concurrent tasks of the AI Core engine is 1. The value range is [1, 13]. Defaults to 1.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Parameter               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
|-------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| is_tailing_optimization | Communication hangover optimization enable in distributed training scenarios to improve performance. By changing a computation dependency relationship, a computation operation that does not depend on the last AR (gradient aggregation fragment) is scheduled to be performed in parallel with the last AR, to optimize communication hangover. ● True: enabled ● False (default): disabled. This parameter must be used in pair with 10.2.2.5.2 NPUOptimizer Constructor and the value must be the same as that of is_tailing_optimization in 10.2.2.5.2 NPUOptimizer Constructor. Example: config = NPURunConfig(is_tailing_optimization=True) |
| horovod_mode            | This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| graph_run_mode          | Graph run mode ● 0: online inference ● 1 (default): training Example: config = NPURunConfig(graph_run_mode=1)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Parameter      | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
|----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| op_debug_level | Operator debug enable. ● 0 (default): disables operator debug. ● 1: enables operator debug and generates a TBE instruction mapping file. In this case, an operator CCE file (.cce), a Python-CCE mapping file (_loc.json), and operator .o and .json files are generated in the kernel_meta folder in the training script execution directory. You can locate the AI Core error by using the line numbers in the CCE code and TBE code of the error operator. ● 2: enables operator debug and generates a TBE instruction mapping file. In this case, an operator CCE file (.cce), a Python-CCE mapping file (_loc.json), and operator .o and .json files are generated in the kernel_meta folder in the training script execution directory, and the build optimization is disabled by enabling the CCE compiler -O0-g. You can locate the AI Core error by using the line numbers in the CCE code and TBE code of the error operator. ● 3: disables operator debug and retains the operator .o and .json files in the kernel_meta folder in the training script execution directory. NOTICE You are advised to set this parameter to 0 or 3 for training. If you need to locate AI Core errors, set this parameter to 1 or 2, which might compromise the network performance. Example: config = NPURunConfig(op_debug_level=1) |

content:
[Doc: TensorFlowNetworkModelPortingandTrainingGuide > 10 Reference > 10.2 API Reference > 10.2.2 TF Adapter APIs > 10.2.2.2.1 NPURunConfig Constructor]

Restrictions
Parameters
In multi-device training scenarios, the save_checkpoints_secs parameter cannot be used to save files by time.

| Parameter                  | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| enable_scope_fusion_passes | Fusion pattern (or fusion patterns separated by commas) to take effect during build. Both built-in and custom scope fusion pattern files are classified into the following two types: ● General: common scope fusion patterns applicable to all networks. It takes effect by default and cannot be manually invalidated. ● Non-General: scope fusion patterns applicable to specific networks. By default, it does not take effect. You can use enable_scope_fusion_passes to specify the fusion pattern list that takes effect. Example: config = NPURunConfig(enable_scope_fusion_passes="ScopeLayerNor mPass,ScopeClipBoxesPass") |
| distribute                 | For distributed training in the PS-Worker architecture, pass the ParameterServerStrat- egy object. Example: config = NPURunConfig(distribute=strategy)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| enable_exception_dump      | Whether to dump the inputs and outputs of error operators. ● 0 (default): disabled ● 1: enabled. Keeping this switch enabled does not compromise the performance. Example: config = NPURunConfig(enable_exception_dump=1)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Parameter               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| op_select_implmode      | Operator implementation mode select. Some operators built in the Ascend AI Processor can be implemented in either high-precision or high-performance mode. ● high_precision: high precision implementation mode. In high-precision mode, Newton's Method or Taylor's Formula is used to improve operator precision with fp16 input. ● high_performance (default): high performance implementation mode. The high-performance implementation mode refers to the optimal performance implementation without affecting the network precision with fp16 input. Example: config = NPURunConfig(op_select_implmode="high_precision") |
| optypelist_for_implmode | List of operator types separated by commas (,). The operators in the list use the mode specified by the op_select_implmode parameter. Currently, Pooling, SoftmaxV2, LRN, and ROIAlign operators are supported. This parameter is used in pair with the op_select_implmode parameter, for example: config = NPURunConfig( op_select_implmode="high_precision", optypelist_for_implmode="Pooling,SoftmaxV2")                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| dynamic_input_config    | Dynamic dimension configuration. Before creating NPURunConfig, you can instantiate a DynamicInputConfig class to set related attributes. For details about the constructor of the DynamicInputConfig class, see DynamicInputConfig Constructor. Example: config = NPURunConfig(dynamic_input_config=dynamic_input_config )                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| mstune_mode             | This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| work_path               | This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| buffer_optimize         | This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| enable_small_channel    | This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Parameter              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
|------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| fusion_switch_file     | Directory of the fusion switch configuration file, including the file name. The value can contain letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), periods (.), and Chinese characters. The system is built in with a range of graph fusion and UB fusion patterns, which are enabled by default. You can disable any rule as required. Example: config = NPURunConfig(fusion_switch_file="/home/test/ fusion_switch.cfg") The following is a template of the fusion_switch.cfg fusion pattern configuration file. on indicates that a fusion pattern is enabled, and off indicates that a fusion pattern is disabled. { "Switch":{ "GraphFusion":{ "ConvToFullyConnectionFusionPass":"off", "SoftmaxFusionPass":"on", "ConvConcatFusionPass":"on", "MatMulBiasAddFusionPass":"on", "PoolingFusionPass":"on", "ZConcatv2dFusionPass":"on", "ZConcatExt2FusionPass":"on", "TfMergeSubFusionPass":"on" }, "UBFusion":{ "TbePool2dQuantFusionPass":"on" } |
| enable_compress_weight | } } This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| compress_weight_conf   | This parameter is not supported in the current version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Parameter              | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| op_compiler_cache_mode | Disk cache enable for operator build. ● enable: enabled. If enabled, operators with the same build configurations and operator configurations will not be built repeatedly, thus accelerating the build speed. ● disable (default): disabled. ● force: forcibly flushes the cache. That is, the existing cache is cleared up before adding new operator builds to the cache. This is especially useful when the Python libraries or dependent libraries are changed. Restrictions: ● It needs to be used in pair with op_compiler_cache_dir. The cache function is enabled only when op_debug_level is set to 0 or 3. ● If set to force, the existing cache will be cleared. Therefore, it is not recommended for parallel program compilation. Otherwise, the cache used by other models may be cleared, causing build failures. ● disable and force are recommended for publishing the final model. Example: config = NPURunConfig(op_compiler_cache_mode="enable") |
| op_compiler_cache_dir  | Disk cache directory for operator build. The value can contain letters, digits, underscores (_), hyphens (-), periods (.), and Chinese characters. If the specified directory exists and is valid, a kernel_cache subdirectory is automatically created. If the specified directory does not exist but is valid, the system automatically creates this directory and the kernel_cache subdirectory. Defaults to $HOME/atc_data. Example: config = NPURunConfig(op_compiler_cache_dir="/home/ test/kernel_cache")                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

Constructor of the NPUOptimizer class, which combines the NPUDistributedOptimizer and NPULossScaleOptimizer optimizers.

It provides the following functions:

- Loss scaling: Loss scaling can be enabled during mixed precision training to solve the underflow problem caused by a small float16 representation range.
- Distributed training: The single-server training optimizer of the user is packaged and an NPU distributed training optimizer is constructed. In singleserver single-device, single-server multi-device, and multi-server multi-device networking modes, gradient aggregation is performed after gradient calculation on devices.
- Communication hangover optimization: By changing a computation dependency relationship, a computation operation that does not depend on the last AR (gradient aggregation fragment) is scheduled to be performed in parallel with the last AR, to optimize communication hangover.

```
import tensorflow as tf from npu_bridge.estimator.npu.npu_optimizer import NPUOptimizer from npu_bridge.estimator.npu.npu_loss_scale_manager import FixedLossScaleManager from npu_bridge.estimator.npu.npu_loss_scale_manager import ExponentialUpdateLossScaleManager # Define a single-server optimizer. optimizer = LAMBOptimizer( learning_rate=learning_rate, weight_decay_rate=0.01, beta_1=0.9, beta_2=0.999, epsilon=1e-6, exclude_from_weight_decay=["LayerNorm", "layer_norm", "bias"]) # Enable loss scaling. if tf.flags.FLAGS.npu_bert_loss_scale not in [None, -1]: if tf.flags.FLAGS.npu_bert_loss_scale == 0: loss_scale_manager = ExponentialUpdateLossScaleManager(init_loss_scale=tf.flags.FLAGS.init_loss_scale_value, incr_every_n_steps=1000, decr_every_n_nan_or_inf=2, decr_ratio=0.5) elif tf.flags.FLAGS.npu_bert_loss_scale >= 1: loss_scale_manager = FixedLossScaleManager(loss_scale=tf.flags.FLAGS.npu_bert_loss_scale) else: raise ValueError("Invalid loss scale: %d" % tf.flags.FLAGS.npu_bert_loss_scale) optimizer = NPUOptimizer(optimizer, loss_scale_manager, is_distributed=tf.flags.FLAGS.distributed, is_loss_scale=True, is_tailing_optimization=True) # Disable loss scaling. else: optimizer = NPUOptimizer(optimizer, is_distributed=tf.flags.FLAGS.distributed)
```

def initialize_system(name = None)

Generally, this API is not required for training. If you want to exclude the GE initialization time in the training time statistics, you can call this API. Before using the collective communication API, you need to call this API to initialize the collective communication.

Restrictions

If the initialize_system API needs to be called and the following functions need to be enabled during training, the configuration must be performed when a session is started in initialize_system.

Table 10-7 Session configuration options in initialize_system
